This is the thing, and its a real problem: people expect internet creators to be journalists or experts. 

Oompaville should not be the one doing an interview to Mr Beast because he is not a journalist. Its for the content, yes, but its not investigative. Its not his fault, hes just a guy as he says and a content creator, but we have to stop outsourcing expertise to "regular people". 
Joe Rogan has the same issue. He is so massive now people equate numbers with expertise. 

This isn't a critique, per say, of oompa, but just more a critique of the modern way of doing things on the internet. 
The question people should be having on all these kinds of things is "what value does this provide society?"
If the answer is entertainment, that is fine, but then its just "drama". 
If its serious investigative work well thats fine too, but thats not for random funny youtube guy now is it?

Author: @harvestcheddar0
Content:
I think people need to be aware of how normal, well adjusted individuals fall into conspiracy theories and extremism. It starts off with the idea being presented as if it makes sense on some level. This happens when there is no push back/no pressure for clarity on what they really mean. People start to think “hey, that kind of makes sense.” The person sees a little more and it starts to increment. Then the next thing you know they are joining a cult, hating random groups of people for no valid reason, and being scammed by grifters. This is why pushing back in interviews is important when you have a large platform.

You don’t have to choose a side to push back. And sometimes one side *is* more rational or truthful than the other. It’s ok to acknowledge that. You can and should push back when interviewing two sides. It might so happen that one side needs more push back than the other. If they are lying more, if they are irrational, etc that will naturally lead to more questions and need for clarification.

Anyway, all that to say I think Oompa is a chill guy who is trying to be open and respectful. Sometimes being too open and platforming certain things without proper framing/pushback can be dangerous. There’s a balance.

Author: @PDjargon
Content:
I feel that there is two sides of the coin for how you could have approached doing the "interview" of MrBeast which one was being basically an interrogator where you wouldn't let MrBeast answer something without it being clear cut answering the question you had (normally only requiring an yes or no answer to TLDR it). Meanwhile the other side of the coin (and what you did) was to have it be more Podcast/chill out talk the chill talk where you provided talking points that you were curious about for MrBeast to answer in his own way and just to get a form of response actually out there instead of being forever silent. 
The crux of the issue/problem I believe is why you've ended up with the massive criticism about it all is that although you roughly said what the purpose of the video was "to provide a meaningful source of information" along with admitting that you aren't a journalist....you didn't hammer it hard enough by repeating it a lot more or saying what the video is not meant to be or your not intending to do (which is to interrogate MrBeast). I think CoffeeZilla's review of it shows this fact the clearest as he said that he found the crypto side very disappointing BECAUSE that's really all he knows about and so could fully criticize only that.

One of the other BIGGEST problems and things that I've seen MrBeast constantly do and pitfall you fell into here is that you let him set the time for doing the "interview" and has it be basically the same day that he approached you about it. Why is this a problem? It meant you were seriously short on preparation time which maybe didn't hit you and so why you didn't spend a lot of time getting questions and points together as you were also a lot more mindset focused on the video you had just released about "retiring" so you can focus on your game. It was so rushed and short noticed/planned out that you didn't know when he would be arriving just that he had got on a plane and it would be an 3-ish hour long flight. Add in the fact you thought that you would have another 2 hours of prep time from presuming he was going to be spending driving over, it's honestly surprising that you did as well as you did with this context in mind but also shows you made the right choice to not be going for the interrogation side of the coin since you maybe don't have the hard line boundries of going "Woha you want to do it today? No we can do it in a weeks time as I need that time to prepare questions and have facts ready."
Just to be clear though, you are not the first this has happened to in terms of MrBeast setting the time frame for the project and being in charge basically of when it's happening rather than it being more of an two way street of "Hey man are you free in 30 mins, I got something I want to show you?" , "I'm busy until 2 so we can meet up then" , "Ah okay sure see you then". The three videos showing this (that I know of and watched) are: William Osman's "How I Almost Ruined MrBeast Squid Game" , Jeff Geerling's "How I almost broke MrBeast's Ages 1-100 video" and finally JLaservideo's "MrBeast Made Me Race Spider-Man Up a Skyscraper!" Content:
In all honesty, it’s fine if you wanted to keep things more relaxed because that's the role you felt YOU should play. And its fair to say there were things you wish you had done differently. It's up to Mr Beast to clear his own name, not you. If he wanted to go over everything in detail with you, he could have brought things up. He could have, and still can, go through each allegation without filtering it through an interview with someone else. It was a choice to have his first time speaking about things publicly be this interview, and every choice since and going forward will be his. 

It's great for you to seriously consider the constructive criticism so you can grow your skills. It’s also important for the people who want to criticize you to do it constructively.
